compatibility.title: Which MG Models Use the E-Tech Electric Motor?
compatibility.intro: The MG E-Tech 110kW motor is MG's entry-level electric powertrain, fitted to the MG4 hatchback and MG ZS EV SUV. It is a permanent magnet synchronous motor with a single-speed reduction gearbox, offering 110 kW (147 hp) and approximately 250 Nm of torque.

failures.title: MG E-Tech Electric Motor Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Bearing wear (rear motor) - 40k-80k miles
items.onset: 40,000-80,000 miles [PATTERN DATA - common on permanent magnet EV motors]
items.whatHappens: Like many EV motors, the E-Tech motor's bearings can wear over time, leading to a whining or droning noise under acceleration or deceleration. This is more common on rear‑mounted motors (RWD MG4) where the motor is more exposed to road vibration and thermal cycling.
items.repairVsReplace: Bearing replacement is a specialist job requiring motor disassembly - typically £800-£1,500 at an EV specialist. If the bearings have failed catastrophically, the motor may be scrap.

items.title: Cooling system leaks - 50k-100k miles
items.onset: 50,000-100,000 miles [PATTERN DATA - EV cooling systems are complex]
items.whatHappens: The E-Tech motor has an integrated liquid cooling system to manage operating temperatures. Leaks in the cooling lines, water pump, or the motor's internal cooling jacket can occur, potentially leading to motor overheating and derating.
items.repairVsReplace: Cooling system repair costs £300-£800. This is usually a repair, not a replacement trigger.

items.title: Inverter failure - 60k+ miles
items.onset: 60,000+ miles [PATTERN DATA - reported on some EV platforms]
items.whatHappens: The inverter converts DC power from the battery to AC for the motor. Inverter faults can cause reduced power, error codes, or complete motor shutdown. This is less common than bearing wear but can be a significant failure when it occurs.
items.repairVsReplace: Inverter replacement costs £800-£2,000. In some cases, the inverter can be repaired by specialist electronics technicians.

failures.goodYearsLine: The E-Tech motor is considered a robust, generally reliable unit. The bearing issue is the most commonly reported mechanical failure, but it typically presents with audible warning (whining) before catastrophic failure, allowing for early intervention. Later production units (2023 onwards) have reportedly revised bearing designs.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the E-Tech 110kW Motor
variants.intro: The E-Tech branding covers several MG electric motor variants. The 110kW unit is the entry‑level motor, but MG also offers a 125kW (MG4 Long Range) and a 150kW (MG4 Extended Range and MG ZS EV Long Range). These are not physically interchangeable. Where to find the code: The motor code is stamped on the motor housing, typically on the top or side of the unit. It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (for EVs, this is the motor number). A VIN decoder will confirm the exact factory specification. Which codes get confused with it: The 110kW motor is frequently confused with the 125kW and 150kW variants - they share the same housing and physical dimensions but have different internal windings, magnets, and inverter calibration. The 110kW motor is standard range only; long‑range models have higher‑output motors. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Fitting a 125kW or 150kW motor to a 110kW car may physically bolt in but will cause battery management system mismatches, incorrect power delivery, and potentially void the battery warranty. Always match the exact motor specification to the vehicle's battery pack and ECU calibration.

relatives.description: Tech 125kW - The higher-output version of the same motor family, used in MG4 Long Range models. It shares the same physical housing and mounting points but has different internal windings and inverter calibration. Not a straight swap with the 110kW unit - the battery management system and ECU calibration differ.
The same basic motor architecture is used across SAIC's EV range, including Roewe and Maxus models. Specifications and mounting points may differ - not guaranteed to be a straight swap into an MG.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement E-Tech Motor - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used E-Tech motor makes sense only if it comes complete with its inverter, wiring loom, and gearbox - a bare motor without ancillaries is rarely viable. The key risk is bearing health and cooling system condition - a used unit without documented history is a gamble. Only buy from a reputable EV breaker who can verify the motor's operating history and provide a warranty.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The recommended route for most E-Tech replacements. A proper recon includes new bearings, new cooling system seals, and a full inverter health check. For a £3,000-£6,000 investment, you get a 12-24 month warranty and a motor that should be good for another 80k+ miles. This is the sensible choice for MG4 owners in the £8,000-£25,000 bracket.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full E-Tech rebuild is generally only justified for numbers‑matching cars or where the motor itself is in pristine condition but needs bearing replacement. Typical costs £5,000-£8,500. For most owners, reconditioned is the smarter and more cost‑effective choice.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted specialists offer supply‑only, supply‑and‑fit, or full workshop installation. Fitting an EV motor requires specialist high‑voltage training and equipment - ensure your chosen garage is qualified for EV work. Fitting through the network includes a 12‑month warranty on parts and labour, with nationwide delivery to your chosen garage or home address.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The E-Tech motor is found in MG4 and MG ZS EV models. MG4 values are typically £8,000-£25,000, where a £3,000+ recon is financially viable and usually sensible. For older or lower‑value examples, consider the battery health as a deciding factor - if the battery is nearing end‑of‑life, the combined replacement cost may exceed the car's value. Always compare the total cost of motor + battery repairs against the vehicle's market value.

It shares the same physical housing and mounting points but has different internal windings and inverter calibration. Not a straight swap with the 110kW unit - the battery management system and ECU calibration differ.

Tech 150kW - The most powerful variant in the MG E-Tech family, used in MG4 Extended Range and MG ZS EV Long Range. It has significant internal differences and requires matching software and battery calibration.
The same basic motor architecture is used across SAIC's EV range, including Roewe and Maxus models. Specifications and mounting points may differ - not guaranteed to be a straight swap into an MG.

The MG E-Tech motor is a unique SAIC design and is not shared with any mainstream European or Japanese EV manufacturer. It should not be confused with Nissan's EM57 motor (used in the Leaf) or Tesla's motor families.

items.question: How much does an MG E-Tech 110kW motor replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned E-Tech 110kW motor typically costs £3,000-£6,000 supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,780-£7,200 depending on labour and warranty. Used units are cheaper at £2,000-£4,000 supply-only but carry higher risk of bearing wear and cooling system health. A full rebuild can exceed £8,500 if the motor requires extensive repair. Fitting time is 8-12 hours at specialist EV workshop rates.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the E-Tech motor?
items.answer: The most widely reported issue is bearing wear, which typically manifests as a whining or droning noise under acceleration or deceleration. Bearing replacement costs £800-£1,500 if caught early. Cooling system leaks and inverter faults are also reported but less common. The bearing issue is typically progressive with audible warning, allowing early intervention.

items.question: Which MG models use the E-Tech 110kW motor?
items.answer: The 110kW E-Tech motor is fitted to the MG4 (Standard Range) and the MG ZS EV (Standard Range). Long-range MG4 models use the 125kW or 150kW variants. Long-range MG ZS EV uses the 150kW variant. The motor is not used in the MG HS or MG3 - those are petrol/hybrid models.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned E-Tech motor?
items.answer: For most owners, a reconditioned E-Tech motor is the better choice because it includes new bearings, cooling system seals, and a full inverter health check. Used units are only advisable if they come complete with inverter, wiring loom, and gearbox - a bare motor without ancillaries is rarely viable. Always verify the motor's operating history and battery health of the donor vehicle before buying used. Only buy from EV specialists with high-voltage experience.

items.question: How do I know if my MG has the 110kW motor and not the 125kW or 150kW?
items.answer: The motor code is stamped on the motor housing and on the V5C registration document under "Engine number". The 110kW motor is fitted to standard-range models only. The 125kW and 150kW motors have different part numbers and internal windings. Check your model badge - "Standard Range" = 110kW; "Long Range" or "Extended Range" = 125kW or 150kW.

items.question: Is the E-Tech motor reliable overall?
items.answer: Yes, the E-Tech motor is considered a robust and generally reliable unit. The bearing issue is the most common mechanical failure, but it typically gives audible warning well before catastrophic failure. Regular cooling system maintenance is essential. The battery is generally more of a long-term concern than the motor itself. Many owners report trouble-free running beyond 100,000 miles.
